questionText: Explain three of the following terms: Smartphones Plan of Action Redundancy Package Curriculum Vitae
stem: AXEL COMPUTERS Axel Computers, an American transnational corporation has had a manufacturing facility in Claragh since 1991. The Claragh plant manufactures components for desktop computers. It has been the main employer in the town since the early 1990s. With the increase in popularity of laptops, tablet computers and smartphones the demand for larger desktop computers has fallen in recent years. As a result the workforce of the Claragh branch of Axel Computers has fallen to 500 compared to 1,300 at the peak of production in 1995. In 2012, the American head office of Axel Computers announced that the Claragh plant will close in July 2013. There is obvious distress among staff and local business people. Although Axel Computers is not as important to the local economy as before it is still the main employer in the town. The Claragh Chamber of Commerce and Claragh Town Council have decided to come together and devise a ‘Plan of Action’ to deal with the closure of the factory. It is hoped that they will come up with ideas and strategies to minimise the negative effects of the closure. Emphasis will be on job creation, training and community enterprise development. Their first task will be to contact relevant government agencies for support. A town meeting has been arranged so that locals can voice their opinions on developments. Mark Ryan has worked at Axel Computers since he left school twelve years ago. He started working on the assembly line and worked his way up to his present position ‘Manufacturing Technician’. Over the years he participated in as many training opportunities and courses as possible. His most recent job involved installing microprocessors into PC’s. Like all other staff of the computer manufacturing firm, he is greatly concerned about the future. He is worried that his lack of a third level qualification and lack of varied work experience will make it more difficult to find employment in the current economic climate. As Mark has worked for Axel Computers for twelve years he will receive a generous redundancy package. He is considering using this money to gain a formal qualification. The I.T. industry is still strong in Ireland but Mark knows that the major I.T. companies operate in the area of software development. He is interested in achieving a suitable qualification in Computer Software Development and Engineering but is not sure how to get the information on the relevant third level courses. Axel Computers, in an attempt to help staff prepare themselves to re-enter the jobs market, has arranged for everyone to meet with recruitment experts. These professionals will advise on Curriculum Vitae preparation and help each worker to devise his/her strategy to gain employment. Axel will also organise support for staff who wish to set up a business of their own.

rows.verbatim: Explain three of the following terms.
rows.contextNote: The paper asks for three of four terms. Keep this one printed choice and every complete model. The paper says Redundancy Package; the scheme heading is Redundancy. No option is compulsory. Keep each response distinct and credit it only once. Complete original guidance: Smartphones: This is a mobile phone/device which has more advanced computing ablity. Some applications which previously were only possible to do on a computer can now be carried out on a smart phone e.g. emails, internet. It can also be used to access phone apps. | Plan of Action: An outline of what needs to be done and by when/by who in order to achieve a particular goal. | Redundancy: A financial settlement paid to compensate employees when they lose their jobs. The payment is based on how long the employee has been working in the firm. | Curriculum Vitae: It is a document used to apply for a job/it gives job seeker’s details such as educational qualifications, work experience, skills, interest/hobbies, referees.

questionText: Mark, as a mature student, has an interview for a place on an IT course. Explain how can he ensure that he performs well at his interview.
stem: AXEL COMPUTERS Axel Computers, an American transnational corporation has had a manufacturing facility in Claragh since 1991. The Claragh plant manufactures components for desktop computers. It has been the main employer in the town since the early 1990s. With the increase in popularity of laptops, tablet computers and smartphones the demand for larger desktop computers has fallen in recent years. As a result the workforce of the Claragh branch of Axel Computers has fallen to 500 compared to 1,300 at the peak of production in 1995. In 2012, the American head office of Axel Computers announced that the Claragh plant will close in July 2013. There is obvious distress among staff and local business people. Although Axel Computers is not as important to the local economy as before it is still the main employer in the town. The Claragh Chamber of Commerce and Claragh Town Council have decided to come together and devise a ‘Plan of Action’ to deal with the closure of the factory. It is hoped that they will come up with ideas and strategies to minimise the negative effects of the closure. Emphasis will be on job creation, training and community enterprise development. Their first task will be to contact relevant government agencies for support. A town meeting has been arranged so that locals can voice their opinions on developments. Mark Ryan has worked at Axel Computers since he left school twelve years ago. He started working on the assembly line and worked his way up to his present position ‘Manufacturing Technician’. Over the years he participated in as many training opportunities and courses as possible. His most recent job involved installing microprocessors into PC’s. Like all other staff of the computer manufacturing firm, he is greatly concerned about the future. He is worried that his lack of a third level qualification and lack of varied work experience will make it more difficult to find employment in the current economic climate. As Mark has worked for Axel Computers for twelve years he will receive a generous redundancy package. He is considering using this money to gain a formal qualification. The I.T. industry is still strong in Ireland but Mark knows that the major I.T. companies operate in the area of software development. He is interested in achieving a suitable qualification in Computer Software Development and Engineering but is not sure how to get the information on the relevant third level courses. Axel Computers, in an attempt to help staff prepare themselves to re-enter the jobs market, has arranged for everyone to meet with recruitment experts. These professionals will advise on Curriculum Vitae preparation and help each worker to devise his/her strategy to gain employment. Axel will also organise support for staff who wish to set up a business of their own.

questionText: Identify a product/service you might like to promote. State and explain three types of advertising that could be used to promote this product/service.
stem: As part of the Leaving Certificate Vocational Programme you are required to organise a class enterprise activity.

rows.verbatim: Identify a product/service you might like to promote. State and explain three types of advertising that could be used to promote this product/service.
rows.contextNote: The scheme gives 3 responses 2 marks each in printed one-mark components. Keep each response distinct and credit it only once. Complete original guidance: Television. Television is very effective and seen by many. Good visuals may be used/cinema | Radio has a large target audience and advertising can be more specific e.g. Radio 1 for an older age group. | Posters/billboards/flyers/buses/press releases. | Special promotions e.g. free samples which can be given out with an existing product or with a complementary product. This is easy to do and provides direct access to the market/stand at a trade fair/celebrity endorsement. | Sponsorship of local event/team. This is good for encouraging new customers and keeping the name fresh. | Run a competition such as writing a slogan for the product. | Newspapers/magazines. | Use of ICT – Facebook/Twitter/Email/Phone apps

rows.verbatim: The scheme prints no answer for this part.

questionText: Outline the steps that should be taken on the day of the visit in to ensure that the event is successful.
stem: Visitors into the classroom are a valuable way of learning about local businesses/community organisations.

rows.verbatim: Outline the steps that should be taken on the day of the visit to ensure that the event is successful.

options: Confirm the time of the talk on the day.
Make sure room is ready e.g set out chairs.
Ensure that refreshments/water are in place.
Check any equipment that is being used eg data projectors/ micro phones/dvd players etc..
Draw up a list of jobs to be done. Ensure that all students with jobs are in school, if not get new people to do them, so that everything is done.
Practice the introduction, thank you’s and questions so that these go well/meet and greet.
Make sure that all class members have a copy/pen to take notes.
Watch the time keeping so that you do not run out of time for questions/get in trouble with other teachers for being late.

rows.contextNote: The scheme gives 5 responses 1 or 0 marks each. Keep all original alternatives.

Complete original guidance: Questionnaire: Can be given to the organization visited as well as to the class Reason: Easy to administer/collate results. Can be completed anonymously.
